speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how many deaths and injuries have resulted from accidents involving migrant workers transported in lorries since the implementation of stricter measures on 1 August 2011; (b) whether the Ministry will impose additional measures to ensure the safety of migrant workers being transported to and from work on their employers' vehicles; and (c) whether the Ministry will consider requiring employers to transport their workers in mini-buses or buses with compulsory seat-belting.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport whether there are any plans to review the carriage of workers at the back of lorries or goods vehicles and, if not, whether LTA intends to introduce any new safety measures to enhance the safety of workers being carried at the back of such vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Last month, there were two unfortunate accidents involving lorries that were transporting workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The first occurred when the lorry ferrying 17 workers collided into a stationary truck along the Pan-Island Expressway (PIE) and resulted in two fatalities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The lorry driver has been arrested for careless driving causing death.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The second incident involved a lorry ferrying nine workers but fortunately, there were no fatalities.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Three days ago, there was an accident between a Police van and a lorry ferrying 11 workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Seventeen people, including five Police officers, were conveyed to the hospital with minor injuries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are deeply saddened by the accidents and would like to offer our deepest condolences to the affected families.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The accidents are currently being investigated by the Traffic Police (TP).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The party or parties found responsible will be dealt with based on our laws.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members have raised concerns on the use of lorries to ferry workers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Countries such as Canada, Thailand and the United States of America allow for passengers to be ferried in the rear deck of goods vehicles travelling on roads, albeit with safety precautions and some restrictions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From a road safety perspective, it will be ideal for lorries not to carry any passengers in their rear decks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But there are very significant practical and operational issues – on top of just cost considerations – which is probably why internationally, it is not an uncommon practice.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to assure Members that we take seriously the safety and well-being of all workers, including our foreign workers, without whose contributions, Singapore would not be what it is today.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As far back as 2008, a Workgroup co-chaired by MOM and LTA conducted a thorough review of the safety of workers being transported on lorries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Workgroup included members from industry associations, the National Safety Council of Singapore, TP and other Government agencies.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over more than a year, the Workgroup studied the issue extensively and consulted widely, including industry groups, safety experts and transport operators.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At that time, companies – especially small and medium enterprises in the construction industry – had strongly urged the Government to allow them to continue ferrying their workers in lorries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The industry associations also provided strong feedback that switching to dedicated bus transport would lead to significantly higher business costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, while lorries can have dual use for transporting workers and equipment, buses cannot and this will result in significant productivity loss.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Other proposals such as using vans with smaller capacities or lowering the cap on deck capacity were also considered, but there were concerns about driver fatigue and therefore, safety, as more trips would have to be made to ferry workers from one site to another.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Workgroup studied the various feedback carefully and laid out a set of recommendations to preserve workers' safety and livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a result, the Government implemented enhanced safety measures for lorries ferrying passengers in 2009 and 2010.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These include fitting higher protective side railings and canopy covers, and higher penalties for non-compliance – up to five times more.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Workgroup's recommendations aimed to protect not only the workers' safety, but also their livelihoods, which was a difficult challenge.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Since then, we have continued to review and refine our regulations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, since 2015, all S Pass and Work Permit Holders are required to pass the necessary theory and practical driving tests before they can obtain a Singapore Class 3 licence that will allow them to drive light goods vehicles, including those which transport workers in the rear decks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Over the last decade, the number of persons on-board lorries who were injured or killed in road traffic accidents has been on a downward trend.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For this year up to March, the injury rate of persons on-board lorries is about 1.5 per 1,000 lorries, comparable with that for persons on-board all motor vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Data for the full month of April 2021 is not yet available.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The number of persons on-board lorries who were killed in road traffic accidents has also been on a downward trend.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That said, declining injuries and fatalities from such accidents should not make us complacent.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One life lost is still one too many.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Back in 2008, the Workgroup had thoroughly considered how to prevent this and many of the suggestions raised by the Members today were previously studied by the Workgroup.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, the Workgroup found that retrofitting seat belts in the rear decks of lorries could result in other safety risks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is because commercially available lorries are not designed for seatbelts to be installed in the rear deck and the floorboards in the rear deck might not be sufficiently strong to keep the seatbelts anchored in the event of an accident.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Worker supply has been disrupted leading to severe manpower shortages.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Projects are already delayed and productivity has been affected because of safe management measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Notwithstanding the improvements made over the years, one fatality and, in fact, one injury, is still one too many.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We appeal to all road users to drive safely and responsibly.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Government will continue to conduct public education so that lorry drivers and owners are reminded of the rules.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA has also been stepping up enforcement to catch errant owners and drivers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We note the concerns regarding this issue and understandably so.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But this is an issue with multifaceted considerations and wider ramifications, including on workers' livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will continue to review the safety rules, engaging the various stakeholders along the way, to see how to enhance these measures further.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Meanwhile, I urge all employers to do their part to ensure the welfare and safety of their staff.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Members of the public can also call LTA's hotline to report any non-compliance with safety regulations.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We often quote trade-offs and costs as part of our decision-making matrix, but for the families in the recent accident who have lost their sons in Singapore, that cost would surmount all other costs that we talked about.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Senior Minister of State spoke earlier about the Workgroup from way back.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of other safeguards, there have been substantial studies internationally on the constraint of speed and how that would impact results out of accidents.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: So, therefore, would the Ministry also consider safeguards such as constraining speeds of lorries for the time being, until new solutions can be found, to perhaps 40 kilometres per hour, so that it significantly improves survivability as well as safety at this speed?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of seat belt, I hear what the Senior Minister of State has said, that the design of the lorries and so on and so forth, but we have done that for the SAF; we have introduced seat belts on our five-tonners.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over and above that, will the Ministry also consider requiring owners and operators to tie down the equipment that they transport together with the workers because it is often these free-flying projectiles in an accident that cause a significant amount of injuries?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have said earlier, every fatality and every injury is one too many.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do want to continue to strive to enhance and preserve the safety of our workers when they are using the roads or when they are being ferried.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But as I have also noted in my answer earlier, this is a multifaceted issue with many ramifications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, even as we consider all these issues, we need to be also mindful that we need to find a balance and calibrated approach in order to preserve the safety of our workers as well as their livelihoods.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the further questions on the various measures that could be taken, firstly, about re-convening the workgroup, as I have said, we have been monitoring the situation since the last review, as well as refining the measures.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We will need some time to engage the various stakeholders and we will take into account all the suggestions and proposals put forth.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We look forward to working with the tripartite partners, the industry and unions on this to find the way forward; a sensible and sustainable way forward.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is already well below the speed limit of 90 kilometres per hour on the expressway.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So further reducing this speed is not recommended by the experts because when you increase the speed differential between the lorries and all the other motor vehicles on the expressway, it can lead to other safety issues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, the increased tendency for overtaking manoeuvres which can increase the risk of accidents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to the study that the Member talked about, it is a Swedish study, which talks about the impact of the vehicle on passengers if an accident were to occur and that it would be less likely to cause serious and fatal injuries, if vehicles were travelling at a speed of below 40 kilometres per hour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, that is really about the impact on the passengers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But here, we also need to consider the increased potential of the risk of accident in the first instance if we were to increase the speed differential.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, as I have said, in the review that we are undertaking, we will consider all views and suggestions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As what the Member said, there may be other areas that we can look into.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to tying down equipment, actually under the Act as well as guidelines issued by the Workplace Safety and Health Council, the employers are already required to safely tie down the equipment or goods, or load the equipment or goods safely, so that these will not be a danger to the passengers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, there are actually guidelines about loading the goods safely.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: If, in fact, the lorries have goods or equipment, then the deck space allowable for ferrying the workers would be correspondingly reduced.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think I have covered the Member's queries.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: First, I would like to thank the Senior Minister of State for her commitment towards safety for our migrant workers.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier that there will be a consultation with various stakeholders.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Because every time we bring this topic up, we hear the counter-argument, saying there will be increased costs.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, we need to actually understand how much costs will be increased by, before we can have a meaningful conversation about whether or not there need to be further safety measures put in place.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The second point that I want to ask a supplementary question on is, the Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier as well that ferrying workers at the back of lorries is actually something that is done in other countries.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: But I note that this is not the case in all other countries.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I would like to know whether a study can also be done into those countries that outlaw this sort of practices and to find out how, what sort of ways they use to overcome some of the costs and practical and operational issues that the Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, as I have noted, when we did the last study there was strong feedback from the industry regarding the significant business costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But, actually, in addition to that, I also mentioned that this, really, is not just about costs, it goes beyond costs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to international practices, as I have also said in my reply, international practices are varied.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, some of these countries that do allow, we think that our challenges are not unique and they probably have similar challenges.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But I agree that even as we undertake a review, we will consult the stakeholders and industries and we will also look at various practices as well as technologies like the Member Mr Alex Yam said earlier.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Senior Minister of State mentioned about projects being delayed in the course of this pandemic.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is a sense out there in the public, whether rightly or wrongly, that construction projects are being hurried to catch up with lost time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: TP, for instance, actually have regular safety talks to the drivers to raise road safety awareness as well as to adopt safe driving habits and we will need to continue to work together – LTA, together with TP and MOM – to reach out, step up public education, sustain public education and to remind them to comply.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, for the companies to comply with the rules and the safety rules and requirements that have already been put in place for workers' safety and to remind drivers of their obligations and responsibilities when ferrying workers.
